subject: biology
title: Calvin Cycle Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll fix CO₂ in the Calvin cycle — the light-independent reactions.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Photosynthesis — Calvin cycle in the stroma, RuBisCO, RuBP, GP, GALP, and regeneration of RuBP.
final_note: You learned that RuBisCO fixes CO2 onto RuBP to make 2 GP per turn, GP is reduced to GALP using ATP and NADPH, one GALP exits as sugar, and the rest regenerate RuBP.

concepts.def: Light-independent CO2 fixation in the chloroplast stroma
Enzyme catalysing CO2 + RuBP → 2 GP — most abundant enzyme on Earth
Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate — 3C triose phosphate; some leaves cycle to make sugar
Provided by light reactions — drive GP → GALP and regeneration

walkthroughs.body_html:
In the stroma:

CO₂ (1C) + RuBP (5C) → unstable 6C intermediate → splits into 2 × GP (3C each).

The enzyme is RuBisCO — slow but plentiful. It's the most abundant enzyme on Earth (mostly because it's so inefficient).

Each GP is reduced using:
- 1 ATP (phosphorylation)
- 1 NADPH (provides hydrogen)
→ GALP (also called G3P or triose phosphate)

Per turn, 2 GP → 2 GALP (uses 2 ATP and 2 NADPH).

To make 1 hexose sugar (glucose, 6C), the cycle must turn 6 times — fixing 6 CO₂.

Of every 6 GALP made (after 3 turns), only 1 leaves the cycle to be used for:
- glucose (via fructose phosphate)
- sucrose
- starch
- amino acids, lipids

The other 5 GALP regenerate RuBP using 3 more ATP.

Bookkeeping per turn:
- 1 CO₂ in
- 3 ATP used (2 to make GALP + 1 to regenerate RuBP per CO₂)
- 2 NADPH used

No light → no ATP/NADPH → Calvin cycle stops. So 'light-independent' just means light is not directly needed.
